He is waiting for you right now near the hall.

Chef, I will not step away from the TV screen.

lines.trans: Fine, I will go and listen to Dmitry Nagiyev.
Good luck to you in the talk with our master!
Keep your eyes peeled and attentively watch the score!

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

вести.gloss: to lead, to conduct (вести себя = to behave)

meanings.en: to lead, to guide, to drive
вести себя: to behave, to conduct oneself
meanings.note: Вы как маленькая себя ведёте = You're behaving like a little girl

examples.trans: You're behaving like a little girl.

examples.text: Лидия Алексеевна, успокойтесь, пожалуйста! Вы как маленькая себя ведёте.
examples.trans: Lydia Alexeyevna, calm down, please! You're behaving like a little girl.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: И, Марина Сергеевна, читайте всё внимательно! Особенно мелким шрифтом!
examples.trans: And, Marina Sergeyevna, read everything carefully! Especially in fine print!
I'm listening right by my ear.
The car is parked near the house.

examples.text: Возле дома Аникеева ходили два подозрительных человека.
examples.trans: Near Anikeev's house two suspicious people were walking.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.en: to hear out, listen attentively to

examples.trans: First listen to me very carefully.
The judge patiently heard out the witness's testimony.

examples.text: Сначала выслушай меня очень внимательно, Аркаша.
examples.trans: First listen to me very carefully, Arkasha.

meanings.note: after 2, 3, 4: года; after 5 and more: лет

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.
examples.trans: That was long ago, thirty years back.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: followed by genitive plural in nominative/accusative

examples.text: Я уже вам сто раз говорила. Я брала двадцать тысяч, вернула тридцать!
examples.trans: I've already told you a hundred times. I borrowed twenty thousand, paid back thirty!

meanings.note: много дел = a lot to do

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?
Understood. And who is managing the dining room?

meanings.note: звать на помощь = to call for help
как тебя зовут? = what's your name? меня зовут ... = my name is ...

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'team; command' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Теперь мы одна команда.
examples.trans: Nothing serious. Now we're one team.
All right, here you go. There, look.

мешать.gloss: to be in the way, to disturb

meanings.en: to be in the way, to hinder

examples.trans: The radiators are in the way.

examples.text: Филиппыч, миксер проехать не может. Радиаторы мешают.
examples.trans: Filippych, the mixer truck can't get through. The radiators are in the way.

meanings.note: From Latin 'momentum' (movement, brief span of time).

examples.text: А мне что-то уже не хочется. Момент упущен.
examples.trans: Somehow I don't feel like it anymore. The moment has passed.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.text: Всё, у меня денег совсем в ноль.
examples.trans: That's it, my money is completely down to zero.

examples.text: Самсон, ты ведь тоже уже в ноль.
examples.trans: Samson, you are also already at zero after all.

examples.text: Наша команда ведёт в счёте два ноль!
examples.trans: Our team is leading in the score two-nil!

meanings.note: Core Russian num meaning 'both' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You both leave here right now.
Get over here right now, quickly, both of you!

examples.text: Вы сейчас отсюда оба уходите. И больше сюда не возвращаетесь. Ясно?
examples.trans: You both leave here right now. And you never come back here again. Clear?

meanings.note: + dative of the person: обещать вам

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

отойти.gloss: to step back, to move away

meanings.en: to step aside, to move back

examples.trans: He stepped over to the window.
Step back! No comment! No comment!
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
Can I go and have a look?
Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: money, a game, a bet, or an election

examples.trans: I lost it on the stock exchange.

examples.text: Денег нет, Самсон. Я их на бирже проиграл.
examples.trans: There is no money, Samson. I lost it on the stock exchange.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

examples.text: У нас с тобой серьёзный разговор.
examples.trans: You and I have a serious talk to have.

examples.text: Есть интересный разговор. Всё хорошо, малыш.
examples.trans: There's an interesting conversation. Everything is fine, kid.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

следить.gloss: to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on

meanings.en: to look after, to keep an eye on

examples.trans: Keep an eye on the child.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('urgent, pressing').

examples.trans: This is a very urgent matter.

examples.text: Яков Григорьевич, у меня срочный вопрос к вам.
examples.trans: Yakov Grigoryevich, I have an urgent question for you.

examples.text: Или счёт в банке. Потому что они все обманщики.
examples.trans: Or a bank account. Because they are all cheats.

meanings.note: смотреть по телевизору = to watch on TV

examples.trans: I'll leave you this television set.
And the television, by the way, is ours!

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Удачи! = Good luck! (genitive: 'I wish you luck')

examples.trans: That's a real stroke of luck.

examples.text: Нет, не получается у меня это забыть. Удачи тебе на новом месте работы.
examples.trans: No, I just can't forget it. Good luck to you in your new job.

meanings.note: играть в футбол = to play football

examples.text: Самсон, ты же опаздываешь на футбол!
examples.trans: Samson, you are late for football!
An important football match is starting.
Tonight is an important football match.

examples.text: У Виктора сейчас начинается важный футбольный матч.
examples.trans: Viktor has an important football match starting now.

meanings.note: person who owns a business or property

examples.trans: The owner of the restaurant came out into the dining room.
The restaurant owner personally greets the guests.
The owner is busy in the kitchen for now.

examples.text: Я не могу гулять здесь целый день.
examples.trans: I can't walk around here all day.
We waited for a whole hour.

examples.text: Илья Олегович! Я не могу гулять здесь целый день.
examples.trans: Ilya Olegovich! I can't walk around here all day.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.
An image appeared on the screen.

examples.text: Иван, посмотрите на этот экран телефона!
examples.trans: Ivan, take a look at this phone screen!

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
